extracted.intended_audience: researchers/faculty/staff preparing revised grant proposals (university applicants to NSF, NIH, or other sponsors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reworking and resubmitting a declined grant proposal to the original sponsor or a different sponsor, including practical steps for responding to reviews and sponsor-specific policies (NSF, NIH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request reviewers' comments and seek feedback from the Program Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal was turned down, request the reviewers' comments and seek feedback from the Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain reviewers' comments to understand weaknesses; consult the Program Officer for clarification and advice. Use feedback from the Program Officer, your colleagues, and the Office of Grants and Contracts Administration (OGCA) to identify improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: If sponsor discourages resubmission, consider alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sponsor discourages resubmission, consider finding an alternative funding source or modifying your project idea or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not persist blindly when the sponsor advises against resubmission; instead explore other agencies or reframe the project to fit different priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond specifically to reviewers' comments in the revised narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond specifically to reviewer's comments in the narrative of the revised proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly address each reviewer concern in the application text (or a response section). Point out changes made to strengthen the proposal in areas judged weak, and clarify information that may have been misinterpreted in the initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point out changes made and clarify misinterpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out changes made to strengthen the proposal in the areas judged to be weak, and clarify information that may have been misinterpreted in the initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resubmitting, call attention to revisions so reviewers can see how critiques were addressed; make clarifications where earlier wording may have led to misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work closely with Program Officer, colleagues, and OGCA
rubrics_metrics.description: You can further your cause by working closely with the Program Officer, being willing to rethink aspects of the project based on the agency's feedback, and being as objective as possible in revising the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage institutional support (OGCA), peers, and the sponsor's Program Officer for suggestions and honest critique. Be open to substantive changes rather than cosmetic edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be willing to rethink aspects of the project and remain objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Be willing to rethink aspects of the project based on the agency's feedback, and be as objective as possible in revising the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid defensiveness; critically evaluate reviewers' critiques and be prepared to change aims, methods, or scope if the feedback indicates fundamental problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF treats each new submission as a separate proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike NIH, NSF considers each new submission as a separate proposal. NSF does not link the new submission to any prior related proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a new NSF submission will be connected to an earlier declined application—a program director may not realize it is a revised version. When resubmitting to NSF, write the proposal to stand alone and address prior critiques explicitly as part of the text since linkage is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF reconsideration process for unfair or improper review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the explanation provided does not satisfy you, you may request that the cognizant NSF Assistant Director or Office Head reconsider the action to determine whether the proposal received a fair and reasonable review, both substantively and procedurally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Grant Policy Manual Section 900 for additional information on the NSF reconsideration process, including the categories of actions that are subject to the NSF reconsideration policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH formal resubmission resources and CSR guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH provides detailed guidance on how to revise and resubmit an application that is declined for funding. The interactive website allows applicants to work through a flow chart describing how to determine whether a resubmission is warranted and permitted, lodge a formal appeal, start over with a new application, or search for funding outside NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH’s interactive resubmission resources and the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) materials to understand the criteria used to evaluate NIH proposals and to decide whether to resubmit, appeal, or pursue other funding avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult institutional OGCA resources for resubmission support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Grants and Contracts Administration (OGCA) may be able to provide suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage OGCA's expertise and shared resources (e.g., pre-award drives, submission guidance) when planning revisions and preparing resubmission materials.
